The group is led by CEO Darius Adamczyk and balances long-cycle industrial exposures with industrial software growth identities [D01].

final.memo:
The Company is a leading industrial conglomerate that the market currently misprices as a stagnant, cohesive whole, failing to recognize the significant underlying value of its separable, high-growth segments [D01]. Despite possessing high-quality assets in warehouse and automation, the company trades at a 17.8x forward P/E, a substantial discount to best-in-class industrial peers like Emerson Electric which trade at 23.8x [D04].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis, based on a blended peer multiple of 22.0x applied to 2017E EPS of $7.25, suggests a intrinsic value of $160 per share [D03, D04]. With the stock currently trading at $124.87, we believe this presents an asymmetric opportunity with significant upside potential [D04].

The market’s skepticism stems from perceived complexity and concerns regarding potential tax and pension complications inherent in a spin-off [D05]. We believe these concerns are manageable and are vastly outweighed by the value creation potential of creating pure-play entities with focused capital allocation [D01, D02].

The recent transition to CEO Darius Adamczyk provides an ideal window for constructive engagement [D01, D07]. We are calling on leadership to initiate a comprehensive strategic review to evaluate the separation of distinct segments and align performance with industrial best-in-class margins [D01, D04]. We expect a clear roadmap for this simplification within the next two quarters [D01].

We are sizing this position at 5% of NAV given our conviction in the valuation gap and the clear catalyst provided by the management transition [D04]. While we maintain index-level hedges to manage beta, we view the 5.3% FCF yield as a hard floor that limits downside risk [D04]. We will act as a constructive partner, but are prepared to escalate if the board prioritizes conglomerate preservation over long-term shareholder value [D01, D02].
